Prologue   Explaining what brought us to the point we find  masrcus .  ONE Welcome Home     He had never understood until that moment what hell would feel like, hell wasn’t hot,  there was no lake of fire there was only the  utter  bonechilling  cold he thought as  his body shuddered feeling more like a seizure then a chill as it  ran through   every inch of muscle and tissue suffering as the nerves became  painfully  aware once again . He could  now  feel the layer of condensation , chemicals and frost   that covered  every inch of his naked body ,  shifting he was quickly and unpleasantly  reminded that  it permeated every inch and every crevice .   He commanded his arm to move and when it finally did, it flopped around like a fish out of  water.   When you wake, your body will take time to recover as your brain relearns to receive input from your senses and nerves, this will be true for your muscles as well, despite being frozen there is a part of your subconscious we believe is still aware on some level and will require some time to reacquaint itself with the body  he heard somewhere from deep within his addled mind.  There had been a briefing he recalled one where they told him the infusion of the chemical would keep the most basic part of his brain alive and working despite his body being frozen, something about needing that in order to revive then it was gone, his mind, like his body in the throes of reawakening.  For what seemed like days he lay there unable to move, unable to command  his body as the painful process of reawakening yes, that’s what they had called it, not thawing reawakening he remembered completed. He remembered their advice  don’t panic  and  give your body time to recover  were the platitudes they had offered before putting him under. Easy for them he thought they didn’t have to fucking go through it.  Eventually his muscles began to respond to his commands, slowly he was able to move his arm, fumbling with the safety catch he removed the harness that kept him in the pod. Then darkness his body exhausted from the simple action,  some time  later he awoke his blurry vision able to tell only that it was still dark  hopefull  still the same dark he thought testing his limbs once again. They responded though not fast and unsteadily they moved like the limbs of an infant they moved in various directions his mind trying to direct them unsuccessfully.  After a while he screamed, he unleashed the pain and frustration and cold pushing it out through his vocal cords until he went hoarse and then blackness again.  The next time he awoke he could see the beginnings of daylight, his vision improved and his muscles  surer , more responsive. Marcus that’s my name, Marcus Gavin he thought as his identity and reason for being there finally resolved in the muddy pit that his mind had become.  Army he thought I am in the army, was in the army his mind corrected as he remembered why it  was  he now found himself, still shivering in this metal pod.  Unsteadily he pulled himself over the lip and fell the ten feet  to the  soft  moss-covered  earth below the pod.  An eternity later he was able to stand, his mind and  body recovering as the sun came up shining through the tall forest  canopy,  he now found himself in.  Where are the rescue vehicles, where are the helicopters  he thought surely even after the event there would be people who would be out looking for him and the others.  For the first time as he stood, his body once again his own he looked out over the lush green unfamiliar forest of earth and took a breath of relief.  Maybe the event had been stopped  he thought seeing no evidence of a global catastrophe, the very reason he had been launched to float in space in the first place.  Marcus slowly began to climb the indents that made the ladder allowing him access to the pod once again. Coming up over the lip he saw the red fabric of the  statis  bed, wires and tubes lay in a mess as they had been ripped off of and out of him when he had  falled .  Hanging onto the edge of the pod, he located the small number pad, taking four attempts to finally enter in the  four-digit  code. Once entered he pressed the green accept button, the stasis bed sliding forward revealing a storage compartment behind it. Marcus climbed back into the pod perching on the still exposed portion of the bed he had spent so long frozen to he began to pull out the  two   medium  black pelican cases and throwing them out of the pod.  Once he was sure he had removed everything he slowly and unsteadily made his way back to the forest floor.  He opened both cases, unsnapping the lid on the first he found the survival pack, breaking the  shrinkwrap  seal  package, he set  it to the side  for a moment  while he excitedly opened the second, a smile of relief broke across his face as he spied the  two packs of shrink  wrapped coyote-tan battle dress uniforms and 5.11 tactical boots.  One he was dressed he felt better and less exposed his mind and body were feeling almost to  there  old self, Standing up he stretched the long limbs on his six foot two inch frame feeling the ample muscles still present from his years of service as a combat military police sergeant in his recently ended army career.  Recent to me he thought looking around again how long have I been in stasis he wondered remembering the one hundred and fifty years he was supposed to have been away from the planet, giving the earth time to heal after the  event. Digging  into the first pack he found the Ontario K-Bar knife and survival hatchet which he clipped on his belt and then smiled again as he reached in and picked up the military m-4 carbine and m-9 service pistol. With an expert hand he checked the rifle, picking up one of the clips he slapped it in hearing the reassuring metal clang as it seated into rifle, pulling the charging handle he loaded a round into the chamber. He looked around finding the biggest tree he could he took careful aim and squeezed the trigger and was rewarded with a dry click looking at the weapon with a curious expression he pulled the charging handle again , expending the round and loading a new one he aimed pulled the trigger and another dry click, he tried it ten more times, then switched magazines and tried it again every time getting the quiet click. “Shit” he whispered pulling the magazine and grabbing a few rounds looking down at his hand he studied them, but they looked normal he thought could it be possible they gave him bad rounds he wondered. Pulling the pistol  and trying that as well click the pistol whispered every  time,  he pulled the receiver and loaded a new round. “Fucking great” he spat putting the weapons back in the pelican case. Was it possible the cordite went bad he wondered, or had they just given him shitty  rounds?  Well hopefully he wouldn’t matter he thought as he looked to the sky hoping to see a spotter plane or helicopter and was quickly disappointed as the only thing that ruled the blue and pink morning sky were the large birds lazily flying overhead.  Well at least I have the knife and hatchet he thought pulling the coyote-tan pack over to him. Unzipping it he began rummaging through the contents until he produced  a black digital radio, on the side it had a simple hand crank allowing you to charge the radio, he cycled the crank for a good five minutes stopping a few times to shake out his hand as the repetition of the action was causing his long dormant muscles to  cramp.He  flipped the power button and was rewarded as the digital display glowed bright green showing it was set to shortwave and displaying a series of numbers. Marcus looked over the simple controls and finally hitting the scan button he extended the two  antenea .  He sat there hunched over the radio as the numbers cycled three times, four times then after ten the green display dimmed. “Dammit” he whispered cranking the radio again until the display lit. Marcus looked to the sky Well maybe  its  too clear to get a signal, no clouds, no bounce he thought remembering his simple training on the radio, shortwave signals can travel great distances bouncing off of the atmosphere repeatedly. He checked the settings and found the one marked  “weather” switching the setting he was yet again rewarded with nothing, not even electronic interference, there was just nothing.  He sat there allowing the radio to die, cranking it back to full power and then repeating the cycle for over three hours as he desperately listened for any sign of civilization.  This doesn’t  mean anything it just means I am too far into the woods to get a good signal   he thought putting the radio back in  the bag  and rummaging through the contents again until he came out with a map, a package of rations and a compass.    He studied the map for several minutes while  sucking on the silver package of what was supposed to be peas, aside from the undesirable green color it tasted more like dirt he thought, wincing as he sucked at the tube again.  He could find no landmarks to orient the map, so he put it back, seeing the canteen attached to the  molle  hooks on the outside of the bag he grabbed it and realized it was empty.  I need to find water he thought which means I need higher ground if I want to find out where the hell to go so, I can get back to civilization  he thought. Packing the bag and zipping it up he hefted it, strapping it to his back and ensuring they were tight. After a few moments he took the pistol and rifle, returning it to the pod’s cargo compartment he closed it allowing the seat to settled back into position and closing the cargo area.    Randomly choosing north Marcus began to walk through the thick forest, avoiding the underbrush judging by the forest growth and the temperature he judged it to be late spring, or early autumn. “Well it could be much worse, you could be  trecking  through three feet of snow there Gavin”  he said smiling at his use of his last name as they had during his time in the army.  In the back of his mind he still couldn’t shake the fear, fifteen thousand people should be landing or landed  based on the briefing they should be doing it around the same damn area he  thought . As the sun rose further into the sky Marcus walked carefully navigating the woods and brush, he could hear the lazy calls of the forest animals and the smell of pine and oak were heavy in the air but he took in the smells and sounds like a starving man would food. Walking through the forest he began noticing things along he trees and ground catching the light. Walking over to a tree he  examines  it closely and to his surprise he found small crystal growths of various colors growing over the large oak’s bark. “Now that’s cool” he said smiling as he ran a finger over one.  Quickly he pulled back his  had  and looked at the little crystal curiously it felt as if it had shocked him lightly or was that just his imagination he thought. Reaching out and touching one again  there  he thought he felt it that time, like a low him of energy “weird” he said studying it for a moment before moving on.  He felt bothered by the crystals, the more he moved north, the more he seemed to notice the glint of the rocks, they covered almost everything. Marcus had grown up in the suburbs and aside from the army had spent very little time In the woods, except for some training missions he thought and never had he seen crystal formations growing all around  so does that mean this is something new, or something that happened because of the event or hell, is it just  Im  in the crystal forests of nowhere  montana  he wondered wryly.  He walked  one throughout the day the longer he walked the more isolated Marcus began to feel. The need to find any sign of civilization become more desperate with every step.  He couldn’t be  alone;  it was impossible he told himself but the further he walked the less sure he was the forest seemed to stretch on forever. Walking over a small hill a breeze appeared, blowing through the trees and rustling the brush. Closing his eyes he tilted his head towards the wind allowing it to  pickup  his blonde hair as he felt it lightly caress his cheeks the feeling calming him as if the feeling somehow awakened some primal feeling of warmth and love as if the hand of his mother were stroking his face. His eyes shot opened as he breathed in the warm air moving through the winds and the smell of mint filled his nose. As a child he remembered playing by an old creek along the shore grew the small mint  plants,  the smell bringing back the memory of that which he needed more  then  even other people, water. He followed the direction of the breeze, catching the heady smell of the small plant here and there on the wind.  Finally,  the forest opened up revealing a small creek. Marcus smiled as he pulled out the canteen from the outside of the pack. On the outside of the cover of the old military surplus item was a pocket, from it he pulled a small blue tablet, filling the canteen he dropped the tablet in closing the bottle and shaking it well  allowing the purification tablet to do its work before opening the bottle and greedily upending the canteen. He refilled it twice, both times ensuring to use the little tablets. He drank until he felt he would burst and finally sated with drink, he filled it one last time  and attached it to his belt where it would be easily reachable, right next to the knife.  Marcus walked north again until the sun began to wane bringing dusk to the lush forest. He had still had no sign of people, he was desperate for any sign at one point he had thought he had caught sight of a deer stand, stumbling through the brush at nearly a run he had come upon the tree to see that it was only a fallen branch that hung in a way to look like a crossbar.  He had not seen any sign that anyone had come through this forest no trash, tracks or tell-tale signs of hunters. As dusk settled over the forest he found a small clearing, he pulled the small tent from the pack he erected the pole fragments into supports and then running them through the loops he quickly had the small blue dome erected he unrolled the small sleeping back that had been attached underneath the pack and pulled out the waterproof matches from a side pocket. It took him nearly thirty minutes to collect enough wood to build a decent fire. It had not rained in at least a week so the wood along the forest floor was decently dry and he thanked his good fortune, the pack only had a limited amount of kindling and he wanted to use it sparingly.  An hour late as darkness had finally come to the forest and the nocturnal calls of the animals began Marcus sat there with the radio trying in vain to hear anything along the channels that would confirm he was not alone.  Eventually  exaughstion  overtook him and he gave up, crawling into the tent he undressed, neatly laying out his clothes for the next day and crawling into the sleeping back.  For a while he lay there trying not to think about what he would do if he found no sign of the others. Instead he thought about his friends from the project, for two years he had trained and gone through treatment after treatment of infusion and gene therapy, the doctors inserting a tube in one artery, pumping his blood into a machine that would infuse his blood with a green substance , something they said would allow him to be able to be revived from Cryogenic Sleep and then the blood, now altered on a genetic level was pumped back into his body. He was forced to do this almost daily for months until they were able to confirm his body had taken to the process. The doctors seemed pleased at his body’s ability to accept the substance and adapt to it. During his time there he had met a few people but of them only three had become friends. Gabrielle Ramirez, Joe Marconi and Victoria Smith. They had been like the four musketeers he thought smiling at memories of the four of them as they heatedly debated anything.  He remembered the day they sat, stunned after a month of entering the  top-secret  project they had been told that humanity would  end,  and they would resurrect it. That was a heavy weight on all  their   shoulders but  leaning on each other had made the news bearable he thought. He drifted off to sleep with thoughts of his friends and slept with nightmares of being alone on earth.  Marcus awoke as the sun began to light the outside of the small tent; he lay there watching as the shadows of the trees played across the fabric like an old Chinese shadow puppet show. Eventually he got up and dressed.  It took him no time at all to disassemble the small tent and secure everything back to the pack, sitting there with the smoldering pile of ash that only the night before had been a pillar of firelight that kept the darkness at bay he sucked at another silver tube, this one said squash but again wincing as he took another helping from the tube and tasting the bitter chalk taste. Before setting off Marcus pulled all of the tubes from the pack and lining them up on the ground and accounting for rationing of two tubes a day, he had enough food two weeks he thought. He needed to find civilization or a lake otherwise he was going to have to learn to hunt with a spear he thought. He packed up the food, taking only two mouthfuls from the canteen he set out again heading north.  Putting one foot in front of the other he made his way through the forest and along game trails, always on the lookout for any sign he was approaching people.  It wasn’t until  mid day  that he his luck appeared to change.  Marcus walked along the small path that from the tracks looked as if deer frequented it.  Maybe it will lead to water  he thought as he walked the  well-worn  path.  As he made his way down the path, something caught his eye the small or medium sparkling of the crystals that still covered every tree, rock and even the ground had become so common place he didn’t even notice it anymore, but something had glinted, not glass or crystal but metal he thought moving past a few trees as he searched the distance for whatever it was that had caught his eye. Then in an instant it happened again, Marcus catching the sight of something  silver in the brush, he broke out in an excited sweat as the thought people ran through his mind. Abandoning his normally safe pace, he sprinted across the woods hurdling brush and fallen trees with no thought to what lay on the other side. He did not take his eyes off of the small view of that silver surface as he sprinted for all he was worth.  Coming to the brush he pulled back the bush that covered it, ripping it away trying to uncover the one sign of mankind that he had  seen since  landing.  Afer  a moment he had pulled away nearly all the brush to reveal another pod.  He stood there his chest heaving at the effort as he realized that his pod had sunken partway into the ground. Marcus leaned in and his heart fell as he came face to face with the mummified body of the occupant.  Once he had seen  that,  he had collapsed against the old relic, sliding down the side of the stained metal to sit in the dirt.  Almost  he thought as tears stained his cheeks, after a time he wiped the tears away, getting up and checking on the occupant. Marcus could see easily what had happened and now he understood why it was buried, the chute had not deployed examining the bottom of the pod he could see the entire underside was crushed from the impact.  Whoever this was had died still in  cryo  he thought looking the  dessicated  naked form of the only other human he had seen.  But where there is one, there are others  he thought clinging onto the only hope that others would have survived. He spent almost an hour trying to get into the cargo area of the pod, but it was too  damaged,  and he had no tools to cut it open. After a  time,  he abandoned it, not wanting to leave a working gun  if one had been in there, but his lack of tools giving him little choice.  He walked north again for the rest of the day, no sign of anymore pods or people.  Waking the next morning he sat in the small tent as a light rain played over the outside of the tent the rhythmic beating of the drops giving him something to concentrate on other  then  his situation. Because of the rain he had got off to a late start and the wet ground forced him to walk more cautiously.  As he left the immediate area of the camp he stopped suddenly and looked down. A set of paw prints grabbed his attention. “Holy shit” he whispered looking at the size of the dog tracks no he corrected himself, not dogs, wolves they were nearly five inches across he had a large pit bull growing up and he remembered the size of its tracks, these were nearly three times that size his mind  tried to calculate how big of a wolf could make a track like that and he quickly realized he did not want to find out.  For most of the day he kept his head on a swivel, every sound causing him to jump as for the first time he  rememebered  something he should have accounted for, this forest had predators and now he kicked himself for leaving the guns, it was irrational, no bullets meant they were simply dead weight but dammit even carrying it would make him feel better he thought,  contuing  his slow progress over the muddy ground.  He walked for half the day, the ground drying  out making  the trip less hazardous. Marcus was beginning to make good time again, the mornings discovery nearly forgotten when the sound of a branch snapping  closeby   stopped  him in his tracks.    Marcus held his breath, listening intently suddenly the overly large paw print very present in his mind as he scanned the brush around him. There it was again another small branch snapped, a scuffling of brush to his left. Snapping his head towards the seemingly innocent sound he studied the trees and tried to see between the leaves in the underbrush and then with a gasp he saw it. A large swath of grey fur passed behind  behind  the brush and then was gone.  His hand reached down without looking away as he continued to scan the area and quietly unsnapped the knife pulling it and holding it close to his stomach as he slowly turned trying to catch sight of the creature stalking him.  Turning the blade so that the blade faced outward, he felt it slip as his palm began to sweat. He desperately tried to remember anything he knew about wild animals.  Don’t show them fear  he thought frantically,  don’t run they will chase and run you down .  Face them they will pause if you don’t act like prey  his mind spat at him recalling anything he could remember.  Then he caught sight of the dirty grey fur as it passed through another swath of underbrush. “Fuck this” he  said,  turned and bolted running as fast as he could. Branches slapped at his face and  body,  but Marcus didn’t notice as he continued to push his body faster his lungs quickly beginning to burn as he tried to run even faster. Then quickly the forest opened up and brought him up short as he found himself on the rocky short of a river. Scanning the  water,  he could see the churning of the heavy current and he whipped his head left and right looking for any way out.  He was trapped, the river  beconing  with its dangerous current slowly  Marcus  taking  a panicked swallow turned and came face to face with the largest canine he had ever seen.  Standing there the large grey wolf loomed as it stood only twenty feet from him. It has to be the size of a horse he thought, his eyes darting left and right hoping to find some possible way of escape. But as he did his situation became worse as two other much smaller wolves, these about the size of dogs and Marcus  realized,  puppies to the mother before him. That must have been the noise, she is training them to hunt, using me for prey he thought randomly watching the two  pad  forward, both similar coloring to the mother except for one had a large black spot on its back. They all three stood attentive and watching as he stood facing them. The mother looked at her cubs as one lowered its head circling behind mother to come on the right side of him, cutting off any possibility of escape. “Fuck, hey mom no chance I can get a pass?” he asked the large creature nervously. She simply stood there, eyeing Marcus as a cat would a mouse, patiently waiting on her cubs he thought . Still holding the knife in his hand, blade out he thought about his chances of actually surviving. He could plant the knife in one or maybe two of the smaller ones, but that would instantly bring mommy and judging by her size he thought the knife wouldn’t stop her before she was able to tear out his throat.  That left one avenue, one dangerous avenue he thought taking a breath and tensing his legs. The  wolves sensed  something,  and he watched as the one to his left crouched a low growl rumbling somewhere deep within the creature.  Marcus spun, took one step and then the  wolve  hit him, he almost fell as the creature launched itself onto his back, fortunately for him they didn’t know what a pack was, the wolf tried to scramble up over the surface of the pack, as Marcus heard the porcelain clack of its teeth near the back of his neck. Knowing he would  lose  his gear and probably his life, he reached up hitting the quick release snaps and dropping the pack and the wolf on the ground as he dove into the chopped river.  The blue grey water filled his vision as the undertow grabbed him, pulling him down stream and refusing to allow him to surface. Marcus rolled across the bottom the current turning him over along the jagged rocks of the  riverbed , he felt the jabs and scrapes as he desperately tried to orient himself.  He felt the breath he held burning in his lungs as he tried to find the surface, the current spinning him over and over.  He held the breath, his chest aching as mercifully, finally his head broke the surface and he heaved trying to inhale the  life saving  air, his body bobbing along the current.  Looking  back,  he could see the wolves, the two pups tearing apart his pack as the mother looked on, watching him with detached interest as his head bobbed above the surface, the river taking him downstream.  Marcus wasn’t sure for how long he floated down the choppy current, doing his best to keep his head above the dull grey chops when finally he made the other shore, pulling himself up onto the rocky shore he collapsed his chest heaving as he tried to  regain his breath and allow the adrenaline that had freely flowed through his system time to dissipate, looking down he spied the  KBar  still in his hand, despite all of that he had managed to hang onto the only real weapon he had. “Thank you for small favors” he rasped then winced when he thought about the pack, all his food and his supplies were now gone. Without food he wouldn’t last long out here. After a  time,  he forced his body up pulling himself off of the rocks and back into the lush forest that ran parallel to the river.  The sun had passed  mid  day ,  so he was able to still orient himself north despite  loosing  the compass and pushed on, walking despite the feeling of helplessness that filled his mind.  He needed to find civilization or he  woud  die of exposure, starvation, animal attack or dehydration he thought pushing his body a little faster as he continued to put one foot in front of the other. Nothing else mattered at this point just taking that step. His entire existence focused down to that one action. There was no past or present, he did not think about the future, the threats all around him or his chances of survival, he just thought about putting that one foot in front of the other.  As dusk approached Marcus found a knoll under a fall tree and did his best to put himself into it, he had no food or fire and he crawled into a semi fetal position to try and keep himself warm. Luckily his clothes had dried hours ago, but the stiff muscles and scrapes from the riverbed did little to improve his mood.  That wolf was too big, what had happened to them, where had these crystals come from, why did they grow on everything and where were the people who landed before him  he thought his  mind drifting to the crashed pod,  had the others suffered that fate, had the parachutes that were packed malfunctioned his being the rare exception  he wondered fear welling deep within him and threatening to overtake him as he forced it down.  As darkness descended over forest and the echoes of the nocturnal animals coming alive in the forest gave him something to focus on other  then  his  sitation .  What would he do if he couldn’t find any sign of people in the next few days he thought and tried to imagine living out his existence alone, deep in the woods and he shuddered at the  thought?  Morning eventually came and he woke to the copper light of the early sunrise as it fought to climb into the sky.  Marcud   climed  out of the bosom of the old fallen tree, stretching his cramped limbs as he surveyed his surroundings.  To his relief he had not come across any more wolves or bears for that matter.  Taking another two swigs from the canteen he secured it on his belt, aside from the knife and hatchet that was all he had left of his supplies.  Hell,  he didn’t even have a way to start a damn fire he thought, but at least with the hatchet he could build a shelter should he need to.  Marcus spent the next four days walking in a northerly direction, at night he would find somewhere to curl into that might give him some protection against a predator. He had come across berries however after eating them he suffered stomach issues for most of the next two days. By that fourth day he was  exaughsted ,  hungry and ready to give up. He was questioning every step why he  continued,  he could not understand what kept him moving forward but he did, one foot in front of the other. The black  BDU’s,  ripped and filthy had begun to itch and the skin on his feet had started peeling the day before. He did not have long until the exposure of the forest and his lack of cleanliness would start to severely effect his health and he knew it.  On that fourth day everything changed the sun had risen to  mid day  and Marcus had  alreafy   slowed,  his progress  lagging,  slowing down every hour he knew it was only a matter of time before he stopped before he finally admitted to  himself,  he was alone.  Cresting a hill his dead eyes scanned the valley below and an open area caught his eye, it wasn’t unusual for the forest to break into small open areas, but this one was different, it wasn’t a simple field but a large path, one that was devoid of trees. Marcus didn’t let his hopes raise, it could simply be another small creek or possibly a rock line he thought, Not taking his eyes off the large worn path that cut through the middle of the woods.  Aside from the river, this was the first major break  in  the miles upon miles of trees and if Marcus was being honest with himself, he thought he would die in this forest.  Getting closer to the break in the  treeline  he could catch glimpses of a worn path. Getting quick views of the muddy area in the middle of the path and there he thought, was he really seeing it or was it instead some kind of trick of the mind. He stopped and stared hard at the path, trying to comprehend what he was seeing. The tracks were narrow and flat,  wheels he thought, not a car like a carriage or wagon something like the  amish  would use or an old hayride like he went on as a kid  he pondered, stumping over a log and catching himself before falling. He moved closer and closer  not taking his eyes off of the tracks.  Then he was there, the tree line falling away as he stood there practically gawking at the mud.  A sound echoed in the distance from his right, quickly growing in volume as he tried to identify the eerily familiar sound almost like a dull series of drum beats the sound considered to grow as he tried to get a look around a corner in the open path. Then all at once they were upon him, horses with riders, actual human riders the clothing they wore looked, odd he thought leather and buckles, swords on  there  hips as the two large black beasts beat their hoofs against the ground. Marcus had been so shocked by the sight of the first humans he had seen since waking from the pod. They had past him by before he found his voice. The whispered croak leaving his throat as they were now riding into the distance “hey, hey wait, please, help” he called his voice failed him, and he watched as they quickly disappeared around another bend. Marcus dropped to his knees as tears freely fell down his cheeks. He was not alone there were other people his mind tried to grasp as he knelt there  crying,  crying in relief in fear and most of all crying in desperation to just talk to another living person.  After a  time,  Marcus got to his feet trying to brush the mud off of the knees of his pants after a while he gave up, the rest of his outfit filthy. But now which way to go he thought, looking in both directions he could follow the  horsemen,  but he would never catch up with them unless they stopped for a day. From the hurry they were in he doubted they would.  But they were coming from somewhere he thought, looking in the other  direction and judging by these tracks people come through here often he judged counting the number of wheel tracks and hoof prints.  His back stiffening with resolve and relief he turned left and one foot in front of the other he walked to find out the source of the fast riders with odd clothing.  He went over in his mind the clothing and weapons they had been briefed on what might happen when they returned but really, swords. Maybe they were honor guards the weapons something carried as decoration he thought. He went over the clothing, the worn leather and dirty buckles these men were not honor guards the clothing they wore spoke of heavy use was it possible that humanity had reverted to the use of bladed weapons, they had no rifles or pistols that he had been able to see. This bothered him and was wasn’t sure the exact reason why and he pondered  this,  taking his mind off his progress. Honestly despite the swords bothering him he was relieved to not only know he wasn’t alone but to have something else to concentrate on taking his mind off of his aching feet and knees.  He had not eaten in days and his water had been gone since yesterday, he was running on fumes and his body could not go on much longer without rest and sustenance.  He walked on, the sun crawling across the sky as the day progressed and finally descending, daytime becoming dusk and dusk finally settling into night. Marcus had lost his flashlight; he had no supplies to make a fire or a torch so doing his best he followed the trail using what little moonlight was available. I am not going to stop, I won’t rest I need to find people, I need to find food he repeated over and over, the mantra  carrying him well past his breaking point as he body, devoid food wanted nothing more  then  to drop then and there. Marcus turned it over  carfully  in his hand, appreciating the way the light played over the blade.  Closing his  eyes,  he reached out with his consciousness and there it was, he felt the sword, it felt odd he thought trying to understand the meaning of it when a familiar voice spoke from behind him. “It is  built  to direct our abilities” and Marcus turned to find Kalman there with a bundle of wrapped blades over his shoulder.  Marcus looked at him quizzically “A what” he asked looking back at the sword. “The four crystals allow you to push your will into it, the blade is tuned to them, it directs it, allowing  you to  aim it and release” he said Putting down the large bundle of weapons and stretching his back. “All of our weapons are imbued with a recipe of crystal powder during the  smithing  process, we have the ability to not only use our weapons to direct our abilities, but we can move arrows in mid-air, use  our will to enhance the swing of the blade or push our will into the shields to reinforce  there  protective abilities” he finished and Marcus looked at the sword in a whole new light.  Then his face fell “How am I supposed to train someone in a fighting style I don’t even know” he asked his friend and Kalman just smiled. “Join me in the training room tomorrow  “he  simply said and then walked out the door leaving Marcus to look after the man.  Marcus and Gabrielle broke for food and rest and it wasn’t until that evening that he returned, the sun had gone down an hour  before,  he walked down the hall the crystal lanterns giving off a warm glow as they lit the way. He entered the Martial hall carrying a lantern as he went,  the  light touching upon the full armory racks. Marcus nodded at the progress he could feel the clock  ticking,  but they were making progress he thought. I hope we can build an army before they come for  us,  he finished the thought and walked over to the desk.  Pulling out the wax  block,  seal and paper he sat  down,  using the example  Agata  had left earlier he began to draft the writs of service.  He rooted around the top drawer of the large desk, finally coming out with sulfur tipped sticks, he lit one and melted wax onto the folded parchment then using the seal, he gently pressed it onto the blob of wax, blowing on it, he cooled the seal and then put it into the building pile.  By the time he was done, there were over two hundred sealed writs piled along the edge of the desk. Marcus walked down to  the chamber where most of the administrative work was done and gave the order for delivery. Within the hour twenty young initiates with bags packed carried an equal share of the writs as they left the keep carrying Marcus’s hopes for a military infrastructure.  Knowing he could do nothing else at that moment he slept a little and then found himself standing with Kalman in the training room. The old man looked tired and he probably was Marcus thought of all the swords he had seen, he didn’t know how many were from the surplus left vs how many this man had crafted, but he was sure that Kalman had not slept much these past few weeks.  Marcus gripped the sword in his hand, liking the way it felt. It was almost reassuring to hold he thought adjusting his grip against the tightly wrapped leather grip.  “Now the first thing you need to understand about a Magi’s blade it is a sword and a bow at the same time, you have the ability to direct you will down the end of the blade, focusing it and making it more powerful. ” Kalman said “ Its  not as hard as it sounds, all you do Is focus your will at the sword” He finished, taking a step back. Marcus looked at the dark metal blade in his hand turning it and allowing it again to catch the light as he considered the man’s words.  Finally,  he reached out, summoning power he felt the heat in his mind he willed fire, directing it at the blade he pushed. Marcus almost dropped the sword as fire shot down the blade  and, in an inch,  wide stream  slammed against the target across the room.  “Holy shit” he breathed looking wide eyed at the smoking hole in the man shaped target. “It focuses the power you send into that stream, building it and amplifying it.” Kalman said with a smile. Marcus absently nodded as he walked over and looked behind the target to see the hole had not only gone through the target, but also into the wall. He had not even poured much power into that he thought shaking his  had .  He should have known, the order had ages before they disbanded  their  military to experiment with crystals and metal, they had found a way for members with medium to low power to  effectivy  use  their  gifts against others.  They spent the whole day practicing and Kalman teaching him how to use the sword, how to swing the sword and how to block with the sword. By the time the sun had begun to set, he was semi competent. But it was a start and he would spend every day working with the weapons, if he was going to lead men, then he would need to  esure  he could fight as good if not better  then  the men he led.  As he left the training room  Karibdis  came to walk next to his friend as they made  there  way down the hall. Marcus was so lost in his  thoughts,  he almost ran into the two women standing in his way. Marcus came up short “ Im  sorry, I didn’t see you there” he said noticing for the first time that the two were Lena and Ela “What would the masters of the Runic and Woodworking guild be doing here?” he asked smiling and shaking hands with the two of them.  “We were waiting for you” Lena said and then nodded to Ela who produced a  box,  as she opened it Marcus could see a myriad of crystal pieces, no bigger  than  a penny each. He looked them over and then raised his head to give the two woman a confused look “ Whats  this?” he asked. Ela nodded down to the box “everyone has a slightly different relationship with the crystals, so we use this to find out  someones  attunement” she finished. Marcus cocked his head “attunement?” he  asked,  and Lena answered “Which crystals respond to you more  then  others” she  translated,  and Marcus nodded thinking he understood.  Lena took his  had  and gently guiding it passed it over the box. Marcus watched as four of the crystals lit up, three of them shining brightly, almost enough to hurt his eyes and the fourth only barely lighting up. With a nod she closed the box and the two women excused themselves leading Marcus there with a bewildered expression on his face.  He had almost made it to his room when an irate Avram caught up to him. “Marcus, come quick, there have been more murders, the church has  began  to strike  against  our   people” he said.  FOURTY - SEVEN Negotiations…     Victoria stood looking out the window as the troops trained in the distance, she could hear the shouting of the trainers as they moved through the  excersize . She smiled as she continued to watch them. Thinking of the gold lioness banner  marching across  the borders of  Lusor  and  Dever , bringing more territories into the fold and bringing the land that much closer to peace, under a single rule, her rule.  She twisted a curl of her blonde hair absently as she stood lost in her thoughts.  “Your  Magesty ” A voice came from the door breaking her out of her thoughts. Victoria turned to see one of her pages. “What is it” she answered letting the annoyance  of being  interrupted shine through the words. The older man winced but pressed forward  reguardless . “Lord Rogan wishes a moment before the negotiations” he said and as he finished the impertinent Lord pushed his way past the man and into the Queens meeting chambers.  He came to the center of the room and bowed to her “My Queen” he said and then  rose,  the first thing she noticed was the wide smile on the  brigand’s  face. She had known Rogan since he was a young man and he had not changed in all that time, he was a schemer, but he was her schemer, thus why she tolerated him. “What is it Lord Rogan” she  said,  moving over to her throne and  gently sitting atop it. She shot the man an annoyed look of which he took no notice.
